# OF3T PROOF PROTOCOL

Written 2026-09-19 by `of3t-orchestrator`, **before any row was dispatched and before any number
exists**. Every tolerance and every pass/fail rule in this document was fixed here, in advance. A
row that wants one changed says so to the orchestrator and gets this file edited, with the change
and its date recorded in §9; a bar that moves after a result appears is not evidence, and a row
that quietly deviates has destroyed the thing the campaign exists to produce.

Moritz's ask, 2026-09-19: *"figure out the most simple way to be completely sure that we completely
reproduce training openfold3 training"*. That is a question about evidence design, so this document
answers it directly: §1 says what reproduction means, §2 says why the honest answer is cheap, and
§3-§7 are the five instruments with their bars.

---

## 1. What "reproduce" means here

**Reproduction is a property of the update rule, not of the duration.** Training is the repeated
application of one function:

    w_{k+1} = U(w_k, b_k, k, s_k)

taking the weights, the batch, the step index and the optimizer/EMA state — **and `b_k` must be
read to include the step's random draws, not just its data** (§4a). If our `U` is their `U`,
then from the same `w_0` and the same batch sequence `b_0..b_n` our `w_n` is their `w_n` for every
n, and running longer produces arithmetic rather than evidence. So the campaign proves `U = U_ref`
and states the bound on that claim honestly (§8). It does not run a training run, and no artifact of
this campaign may be described as one.

## 2. Why this is cheap: `U` factorises, and only one factor needs the device

The single most useful thing in this protocol. `U` decomposes into five components, and **four of
the five are state-free or model-free and can be verified exactly, on CPU, over their whole
domain** — not sampled, not estimated:

| # | Component | Nature | Instrument | Needs a card |
|---|-----------|--------|-----------|--------------|
| 1 | Gradient `g = dL/dw` | model-dependent | A: per-parameter vs float64 | **yes** |
| 2 | LR schedule `lr(k)` | pure function of `k` | B: exact, whole domain | no |
| 3 | Grad clipping / `grad_manager` | pure function of `(g, cfg)` | B: exact, straddling cases | no |
| 4 | Optimizer `AdamW` + fp32 master | closed-form recurrence | C: injected-gradient drive | no |
| 5 | EMA | closed-form recurrence | C: injected-gradient drive | no |

Components 2-5 carry no model and no device. Driving them with a **synthetic, injected** gradient
sequence verifies them **better** than an N-step training trajectory does, because the input is
controlled: a trajectory that agrees tells you nothing about which factor was right, while an
injected drive isolates each one and can be pushed through its corner cases (the clip threshold, the
warmup knee, a zero gradient, a disabled parameter) that a real batch will never happen to hit.

**Instrument D, their own test, added 2026-09-19 (§9/A3).** `openfold3/tests/test_training_full.py`
exists in **0.5.0**, not in the 0.4.3 that tt-bio pins — 210 lines driving the real
`run_openfold train --runner-yaml` console script and asserting exit 0 plus a written `.ckpt`.
Their `ModelRunner.__init__` takes `model_class` and does `self.model = model_class(self.config)`
(`core/runners/model_runner.py:51`), with `training_step` being `self.model(batch)` then
`self.loss(...)`. **One injection point, and their loss, LR schedule, `grad_manager`, optimizer
and EMA all stay theirs**, which is what makes "their test, our model" an artifact rather than a
rewrite. It is complementary to instruments A-C, not a substitute: it proves the assembly runs
under their own harness, while A-C prove the arithmetic. As shipped it reports **2 skipped,
"Requires cuda; found cpu"** (`@skip_unless_cuda_available`), and **a module-skip is not a pass** —
whatever is skipped is reported as skipped, and the skip is addressed openly rather than patched
away in silence.

This is why N does not have to be large, and it is the answer to "the most simple way to be
completely sure": **verify the state-free factors exactly and analytically; spend the scarce device
time only on the gradient; then run a short N-step trajectory as an integration test whose job is to
catch wiring, not arithmetic.**

## 3. Instrument A — per-parameter gradient equivalence (the device-side proof)

One step, identical initialisation, identical batch, our stack against the float64 reference.

### 3a. The comparison space, which is a real problem and is settled here

**Our OF3 is an independent ttnn reimplementation, not their code on our backend** (`NOTICE:53-56`).
Our parameters are therefore not in bijection with theirs: `tt_bio/protenix_weights.py:25-26` fuses
their `linear_a_g.weight` and `linear_b_g.weight` into our single `g_in.weight` by
`torch.cat(..., dim=0)`, and the same for `linear_a_p`/`linear_b_p` into `p_in.weight`, at every
triangle-multiplication module in the trunk, the MSA stack and the template stack.

**Decision: the comparison is made in THEIR parameter space.** Our fused gradient is split back
along dim 0 at the fusion boundary and each half compared against their corresponding tensor. Two
reasons, both binding: a fused comparison lets one half's agreement mask the other half's error, and
their space is the space the claim is about. The split is exact — concatenation along dim 0 is
losslessly invertible — so it contributes no tolerance of its own.

**Deliverable, published before any gradient is compared:** a *bijection manifest* mapping every one
of their parameter tensors to exactly one `(our tensor, slice)` pair, with the unmapped set on
**both** sides enumerated and individually explained. An unexplained unmapped tensor is a failure of
this instrument, not a footnote. A per-parameter claim over a map that silently drops tensors is the
same defect as a mean hiding an outlier.

### 3b. A missing gradient and a zero gradient are different, and must stay different

Their runner disables the confidence-head parameters whenever a sample's total confidence weight is
zero (`projects/of3_all_atom/runner.py:364-386`), which the initial-training stage config does for
four of its five datasets (§6). On such a batch their confidence parameters have **no gradient**,
not a zero one.

**Rule: `None` must match `None`, and a zero gradient must match a zero gradient.** Filling a
missing gradient with `zeros_like` to make the comparison run is forbidden. That exact substitution
has already cost this fleet a campaign — memory `zero-filled-missing-gradient-hides-an-untrained-
model`: the optimizer stepped anyway, `grad_norm` stayed plausible and even declined, 4,124 tests
stayed green, and 99.97 % of the model never trained. The gradient-presence pattern is compared as
a set, per parameter, before any magnitude is compared.

### 3c. The reference, and what it is verified against

The reference is **float64**, and it is itself validated by **float64 central finite differences**
before anything is compared to it. Never against another approximation, and never against a
reference that could share our misunderstanding. PTX's SDPA backward is the precedent and the
warning: its kernel adds the mask **before** the scale — `softmax((q@k^T + mask) * scale) @ v` — and
a reference written the conventional way agrees with a *wrong* gradient while both disagree with the
forward. Every reference in this campaign is validated against the forward it claims to
differentiate, then against finite differences, then used.

### 3c-bis. Finite differences CANNOT validate a recycled trunk gradient — added 2026-09-19 (§9/A11)

§3c requires every reference to be validated by float64 central finite differences before
anything is compared to it. For OpenFold3's trunk **that validation is not merely noisy, it is
measuring a different function**, and `of3t-reference` established it with four independent
signatures.

Their trunk runs **`num_recycles + 1` passes over the same weights and tapes only the last**
(`model.py:230`, `enable_grad = is_grad_enabled and is_final_iter`). So:

- a **finite difference perturbs the weight in every cycle** and measures the **total**
  derivative;
- the **analytic gradient is deliberately the partial** derivative through the final cycle only.

They are different quantities and no choice of `h` reconciles them. The evidence, all four
consistent with that and with nothing else: the difference quotient is **flat from h = 1e-3 to
1e-6** where a truncation error would fall; it is **larger than analytic**; the factor is
**entry-specific** (5.95x on `pairformer_stack.blocks.2.tri_mul_in.layer_norm_in.bias`, 1.53x on
`blocks.41.tri_mul_out.linear_a_g`); and it is **absent outside the recycling loop**, where
diffusion-module entries converge properly — 1.785e-08 at h = 1e-4 rising to 1.204e-05 at
h = 1e-7 as roundoff takes over, which is exactly the shape a healthy sweep has.

**The rule: run the finite-difference validation at `num_recycles = 0`**, where the taped and
untaped functions coincide. A disagreement at a higher recycle count is **not** evidence of a
defect and must not be reported as one — nor may it be used to pass a reference, since at
`num_recycles = 0` the check is real and at 3 it is vacuous in the other direction.

**This also sharpens §4a.** The recycle count is not only an input to be matched across stacks:
**it changes what the gradient means.** A reference taken at 3 recycles compared against ours at
0 would disagree for this reason with no bug anywhere, and the disagreement would look exactly
like a trunk defect.

### 3d. The bars, fixed now

Metric per tensor: relative L2, `||g_ours - g_ref||_2 / (||g_ref||_2 + 1e-30)`, computed in float64
after the split of §3a. Report also the per-element max relative deviation, and always the **worst
tensor by name and location** — never a mean, never a norm over all parameters, never a sample.

- **Per-tensor bar: 5.0e-02.**
- **Median-over-tensors bar: 2.0e-02.**

Justification, recorded before results exist. **bfloat16 keeps 7 explicit mantissa bits, so its
precision is 8 bits including the implicit leading one: the ulp at 1.0 is 2^-7 = 7.8e-03 and the
unit roundoff — half an ulp under round-to-nearest, which is the bound on a single relative
rounding error — is 2^-8 = 3.9e-03.** (Corrected 2026-09-19: this section first said "8 mantissa
bits", which is the wrong phrasing for the right constant. **The bar does not move**, because
accumulated rounding is bounded by the unit roundoff and not by the ulp, and 3.9e-03 was always
the unit roundoff. `of3t-gradients` caught the same slip in its own displacement note, where the
ulp *was* the right quantity and 3.9e-03 was wrong.) The trunk composes 48 pairformer blocks; error through a depth-d chain of
well-conditioned operations grows about sqrt(d), and sqrt(48) x 3.9e-03 = 2.7e-02, which is the
scale the bf16 floor alone predicts. The median bar is set just under that floor because most
tensors sit far shallower than the deepest path; the per-tensor bar is one doubling above it, so a
tensor that exceeds 5.0e-02 is doing something bf16 rounding does not explain. For calibration, PTX
measured its single-op SDPA backward at dq 6.37e-03 / dk 6.40e-03 / dv 6.02e-03 / dbias 6.35e-03
against a float64 reference validated by central finite differences to 1.76e-09.

**A tensor over the bar is the finding.** It is localised, explained and reported. It is never a
reason to move the bar, and no row may move one.

### 3d-bis. The §3d bars govern GRADIENTS. Forward comparisons are a different instrument. (Added 2026-09-19, §9/A6 — no bar moved.)

`of3t-confidence` applied the 5.0e-02 per-tensor bar to a **forward activation** and reported
`plddt_logits` at **2.424e-01** as a miss. Applying it there was conservative and correct of the
row, and the clarification below is not a response to the number: **no gradient bar moves, and
this section adds a requirement rather than relaxing one.**

The §3d bars were derived for gradients — bf16 unit roundoff 3.9e-03 composed over a 48-block
trunk. A forward activation read at the output of a head that **amplifies by 26x** is a
different quantity with a different error budget, and §3c's role for a forward is to **validate
a reference before its gradient is trusted** (the mask-before-scale discipline), not to pass or
fail an activation.

**So a forward miss is neither a pass nor a failure on its own. It is a pointer, and it obliges
two measurements:**

1. **The downstream quantity the model and the loss actually consume**, not the logits. For
   pLDDT that is the per-residue confidence after the softmax and bin expectation, and the
   cross-entropy loss value. A large relative L2 on logits can be a negligible shift in the
   score, or it can be a real one; the logits do not say which, and only the consumed quantity
   is comparable against Moritz's standing bar — **parity means accuracy, not bit-exactness**.
2. **The gradient**, which is what §3d governs and what a training reproduction rests on. A
   forward that is imprecise but whose gradient is inside the bar does not block training
   equivalence. A forward that is *wrong* rather than imprecise does, and that is a hard stop.

If the consumed quantity or the gradient misses, **that is the finding** and it is reported as
one, with no bar moved.

### 3e. The bars must be shown to be capable of failing

Before any pass is claimed, a **negative control**: perturb exactly one parameter's gradient by 1 %
and confirm the check fails, on that tensor and only that tensor. A gate nobody has watched fail is
not a gate (memory `negative-control-must-break-what-check-reads`), and its sibling failure is
already on this fleet's record — a parity gate that built both sides from one source, where an empty
model agreed with an empty model to every bit. The question each instrument must answer in writing:
**which check fails if our model is replaced by zeros?**

## 4. Instrument B — the state-free functions, verified exactly

**The LR schedule.** `AlphaFoldLRScheduler` (`core/utils/lr_schedulers.py`) is linear warmup, then a
plateau, then exponential decay, and it is a **pure function of the step index** with no state
beyond its configuration. It therefore needs no trajectory at all: evaluate ours and theirs in
float64 at every knee and on both sides of each — steps 0, 1, 999, 1000, 1001, 49999, 50000, 50001,
99999, 100000, 100001 for the default `warmup_no_steps=1000`,
`start_decay_after_n_steps=50000`, `decay_every_n_steps=50000` — plus 1000 uniformly spaced interior
points. **Bar: exact float64 equality**, because both sides compute the same closed form and there
is no accumulation to excuse a difference. This is a complete proof of the schedule, over its whole
domain, and it is strictly stronger than anything an N-step run can show.

**Gradient clipping and `grad_manager`** (`core/utils/grad_manager.py`, 406 lines). A pure function
of the gradients and the configuration. Verified on **synthetic** gradient vectors constructed to
straddle every branch: just under the clip threshold, exactly at it, just over, a zero gradient, a
non-finite gradient, the per-sample-clipping path, and the disabled-parameter path of §3b. Corner
cases a real batch reaches only by luck are reached here by construction, which is the point of
the instrument.

**Bar, corrected 2026-09-19 (§9/A7 — a number already existed when this was written, and it is
marked as such).** This section originally said *relative 1e-12 in float64 on the scaling factor*.
**That bar is unachievable by construction and was mis-specified**, not missed: both stacks
compute the global norm in **float32** — theirs at `grad_manager.py:49` (`p.grad.float()`), ours
in `optim.py`'s `grad_norm()` — and they **associate the sum differently**, theirs as a norm over
stacked per-tensor norms and ours as a running sum of per-tensor dot products. Float32 unit
roundoff is 2^-24 = **5.96e-08** and a sum of squares over N elements carries about sqrt(N) of it,
so the floor for a ~100-element case is of order **6e-07**. No two float32 implementations with
different association order can agree to 1e-12, so the original figure could only ever have been
failed and failing it would have said nothing about the code.

The bar for this instrument is therefore the **dtype-derived float32 floor, 6e-07**, and the
derivation above uses only the dtype and the element count — **not** the values that were
measured. The instrument reports against **both** figures so the original is still visible, and
its negative control must clear the float32 floor by a wide margin to count.

This correction applies to **this instrument only**. §4's LR-schedule half keeps exact float64
equality, because there both sides evaluate the same closed form with nothing accumulated. No
gradient bar in §3d changes.

### 4a. The per-step random draws are part of the update rule — added 2026-09-19, see §9/A4

`of3t-perf` established from their `model.py` that **in training the trunk recycle count is drawn
per step from U{0..3} via a synced generator**, where inference pins it at 3. And
`_train_diffusion` differentiates 48 noised structures per step in `initial_training`, 32 in the
finetunes — draws again.

So a training step's work is not determined by its batch. Two consequences, both binding:

- **For equivalence.** The RNG streams are inputs to `U` and must be pinned and matched across
  stacks exactly as the batch and the data order are. A trajectory comparison in which the two
  stacks drew different recycle counts is comparing different amounts of work and is void, and it
  will not announce itself — it looks like a divergence in the weights. The frozen bundle records
  the drawn recycle count and the diffusion noise per step, and the comparison asserts them equal
  before comparing anything else.
- **For timing.** Every s/step figure states the drawn recycle count it was measured at, pinned,
  alongside the clock, the board class, the per-rank batch and the crop. **A figure quoted
  without it is a sample from a distribution over U{0..3}, not a measurement**, and the spread is
  large because a recycle is a whole trunk pass.

Note our stack already anticipates the gradient scoping: `tt_bio/ops.py` carries a recycle hook
whose comment states that a recycling stack differentiates its LAST cycle only, "AF3's own
training structure, and the difference between a tape holding one cycle and a tape holding ten of
them". Their `enable_grad = is_grad_enabled and is_final_iter and not train_confidence_only`
confirms it from their side. **Taping all cycles is therefore both wrong and expensive** — it
computes a gradient that is not theirs and holds several times the activations.

## 5. Instrument C — the optimizer and the EMA, driven by injected gradients

**Their optimizer is `torch.optim.Adam`, not AdamW** (`runner.py:854`) — no weight decay. This
protocol said AdamW until `of3t-equivalence` checked; corrected 2026-09-19 (§9/A5). Our defaults
are Protenix's and all three differ: weight_decay 0.01, beta2 0.999, lr 3e-4 against OF3's **0.0,
0.95, 1.8e-3**. An OF3 recipe that does not pin all three trains a different update rule with
every metric looking healthy.

**The EMA is NOT on the update path, established 2026-09-19 from their source (§9/A8).** It is
updated at `on_train_batch_end`, *after* `optimizer.step()`, reading **from** the model
(`runner.py:769`); it is read back into the model only at `on_validation_epoch_start`
(`runner.py:599`), and the training weights are cloned into `self.cached_weights` first and
restored at `on_validation_epoch_end` (`runner.py:833-834`). Its rule is
`copy = decay*copy + (1-decay)*param`. So the EMA is a **pure downstream observer of the training
trajectory**: `w_{k+1}` does not depend on it, and its absence cannot change a weight trajectory.

What that does and does not license. It means **the missing EMA does not block update-rule
equivalence**, which is this campaign's claim, and an N-step trajectory comparison is valid
without it. It does **not** mean the EMA is unimportant: validation metrics are computed on EMA
weights, and if a published checkpoint is the EMA copy then landing on the same final weights
needs it. Those are claims about eval and about checkpoints, not about the update rule, and
they are listed in §8's DOESNOT rather than quietly dropped.

`Adam` over an fp32 master, and the EMA (`runner.py:768-769`, decay 0.999, updated every step), are
state-carrying recurrences but closed-form ones. Verify them **decoupled from the model entirely**:
feed both implementations the identical synthetic gradient sequence for 200 steps and compare the
parameter state at every step.

This isolates optimizer-state divergence from gradient divergence, which a trajectory run
structurally cannot. 200 steps is affordable because no model runs, and it crosses the warmup knee
at 1000 only if configured down — so the drive is run **twice**, once with the shipped configuration
and once with `warmup_no_steps` scaled so all three knees fall inside the 200 steps. **Bar: relative
1e-06 per parameter per step in fp32 master precision**, which is the fp32 master's own floor and
not a bf16 argument, because nothing here is bf16.

## 6. Coverage — where reproductions quietly fail, made falsifiable

A gradient match on a batch that never triggered the confidence loss or the template path proves
nothing about them. Coverage is **demonstrated by instrumentation, never argued**.

**The finding that shapes this requirement: no single stage of theirs fires every loss term.** Their
loss weights are per-dataset overrides inside each stage config, and they arrive per-example in the
batch (`batch["loss_weights"]`, `runner.py:448`). Measured from `examples/training_yamls/`:

- `initial_training.yml` — zeroes `experimentally_resolved`, `plddt`, `pae`, `pde` on 4 of its
  datasets; only the `weighted-pdb` dataset leaves them at the base default. Crop 384.
- `finetune_1.yml`, `finetune_2.yml` — `bond: 4.0`, `smooth_lddt: 0.0`; the same four confidence
  terms zeroed on 4 datasets. Crops 640 and 768.
- `finetune_3.yml` — `mse: 0.0`, `distogram: 0.0`, `smooth_lddt: 0.0`, `pae: 1e-4`. The
  confidence-only stage. Crop 768.

So the coverage requirement is **the union over stages, with a named (stage, dataset) pair carrying
each term**, not "all terms in one run". For every loss term and every conditional path — templates,
MSA, the confidence heads, the diffusion rollout, the disabled-parameter path — the row names the
`(stage, dataset)` that fires it, and proves it fired by instrumentation showing a **non-zero weight
AND a non-zero contribution to the gradient**. A term whose weight is non-zero but whose gradient
contribution is zero has not been covered; it has been skipped with extra steps.

**Coverage is measured at RUNTIME, not statically — amended 2026-09-19, see §9/A2.** A static
census of which ttnn verbs a file calls is a useful screen and nothing more. `of3t-perf` found the
reason it is not sufficient: `tape()` installs itself by rebinding the module-global name `ttnn`,
and `openfold3_confidence.py:163` and `openfold3_host_prep.py:219` do `import ttnn` **inside a
function**, which binds the real module into the function's scope at call time. Those 16 call
sites run untaped no matter what the swap did, and because they are handed raw handles rather
than `autograd.Tensor`s, **nothing raises**. The tape's guarantee that an op it cannot follow is
loud does not cover this shape of gap. So every coverage claim in this campaign is backed by a
census taken **during a real taped forward**, counting calls that actually routed, and a
file-level check that no module reachable from the training path imports `ttnn` inside a function.

Any path that cannot be fired is listed in the coverage table as **NOT COVERED**, with the reason.
An honest gap is a result. A silent one voids the proof.

## 7. The N-step trajectory — an integration test, not the load-bearing proof

With §4 and §5 verifying the schedule, the clipping, the optimizer and the EMA exactly, the N-step
trajectory has one job left: catch **wiring** — a component applied in the wrong order, called at
the wrong time, fed stale state, or not called at all. That is what it is good at and it does not
need to be long to do it.

**N = 20**, fixed now. It exceeds the gradient-accumulation cycle length so clipping and optimizer
state engage, and every step of it sits inside the 1000-step linear warmup, so the LR changes on
every one of the 20 steps and a wrong or frozen schedule shows immediately.

### 7a. Compare the weight DELTA, not the weights — amended 2026-09-19, see §9/A1

`of3t-reference` measured that `AlphaFoldLRScheduler` is constructed with `last_epoch=-1`, so
`_LRScheduler.__init__` calls `step()` once and **the first optimizer step runs at lr = 0.0**.
Measured on a 2-element parameter with grad 1.0: step 1 lr=0 delta=0; step 2 lr=1.8e-06
delta=1.79e-06; step 3 lr=3.6e-06 delta=3.58e-06.

That finding generalises into a defect in this protocol as first written, and the correction is
load-bearing. With warmup over 1000 steps to `max_lr=1e-3` from `base_lr=0`, the LR at step k is
about `k x 1e-6`, so **20 steps move the weights by a relative amount of order 1e-4**. A relative
L2 computed on `w_k` is therefore dominated by `w_0`, which is identical on both stacks **by
construction** — it would read ~0 for a correct implementation and ~0 for one computing garbage.
Comparing weights would have made this entire instrument vacuous.

**The compared quantity is the update, `d_k = w_k - w_0`**, per tensor, as
`||d_k_ours - d_k_ref||_2 / (||d_k_ref||_2 + 1e-30)`. That is the quantity the update rule
produces and the only one carrying information at these step sizes.

**Step 1 is non-discriminating only when BOTH sides read zero — corrected 2026-09-19 (§9/A10).**
At k=1 the LR is exactly zero, so a **correct** implementation has `d_1 = 0` and any two correct
implementations agree bit-exactly, including with one computing garbage. That is why it cannot
be quoted as a pass.

But it is not free of information. `of3t-gradients` measured **our `d_1` at 0.0139 where theirs
is exactly 0**, because `recipes.py:119` wires `af3_lr(s)` while `AdamW.step` increments before
it reads — **our step 1 runs at `lr(1)` where theirs runs at `lr(0)`**. So a **non-zero `d_1` is
itself the finding**: it cannot indicate agreement, and it does indicate an off-by-one in the
schedule wiring. Report `d_1` for both sides and treat any non-zero value as a defect to
localise, not as a rung to skip.

**Discrimination starts at k = 2, corrected 2026-09-19 (§9/A9).** This section first excluded
k=2 as well, on the reasoning that the update there is ~1.8e-06 *relative to the weights* and
"reads the tolerance". That conflated the **size** of the update with the **precision of
comparing it**. `of3t-reference` measured the quantity that actually matters: `d_1 = 0` exactly,
but **`d_2 = 7.309e-04`** in absolute terms — a real, non-zero update whose relative comparison
between two stacks is perfectly well-posed. Relative displacement against `||w_0|| = 1251.30` is
5.84e-07 at k=2 and 2.13e-03 at k=20, and neither figure bears on whether `d_2` can be compared.
**Fit the growth law over k = 2..20**; only k=1 is excluded.

**The trajectory is run twice.** Once with the shipped configuration, and once with
`warmup_no_steps` scaled down so the 20 steps produce updates of order 1e-2 relative. The second
run is what gives the growth law a usable dynamic range; the first is what shows the shipped
configuration is the one being reproduced. Neither is optional and the scaled run is a
configuration change, not a change to the update rule — `warmup_no_steps` is a knob they expose.

### 7a-bis. What the trajectory structurally CANNOT see, and why instrument A is not optional

`of3t-equivalence` measured the sharpest available argument for this protocol's shape, and it
belongs here rather than in a row's report. **Adam is invariant to a uniform per-tensor scaling
of the gradient.** Scaling one tensor's gradient by 1.01 at *every* step moved the weight
trajectory by **2.547e-07** — three orders under the bar, completely invisible — because
`m_hat / (sqrt(v_hat) + eps)` cancels the common factor.

So a whole class of gradient error is **structurally undetectable downstream of Adam, at any
trajectory length**. No N makes §7 see it. That is the reason instrument A compares gradients
per parameter directly rather than inferring their correctness from where the weights ended up,
and it is the reason a longer run would not have been better evidence. Any future proposal to
drop or shorten instrument A in favour of "just run more steps" is answered by this number.

### 7b. What to report

1. `d_k` divergence per step, per tensor, as relative L2, for k = 1..20, with **k = 1** labelled
   non-discriminating (`d_1 = 0` exactly);
2. the **first tensor to move** beyond the §3d bar, and at which step;
3. the **growth law** of the divergence in k, fitted over k = 2..20 (§9/A9).

**The bar is the growth law, and this is the criterion that matters.** Per-step divergence within
the §3d bars is expected and is bf16 noise. Divergence that grows **linearly or sub-linearly** in k
is that noise accumulating and passes. Divergence that grows **super-linearly or geometrically** in
k fails, at any magnitude, including magnitudes inside the bars — that signature is a different
update rule, not a rounding difference, and it is the one thing a single-step gradient check cannot
see.

## 8. What this protocol proves, and what it does not

**PROVES.** That our training step is their training step: per-parameter gradient equivalence in
their parameter space against a finite-difference-validated float64 reference, with full loss-term
and conditional-path coverage; the LR schedule exactly over its whole domain; the clipping, the
optimizer and the EMA exactly under controlled drive; and the assembled update rule over 20
consecutive steps from identical init and identical data order, with a bounded growth law.

**DOES NOT PROVE.** Anything about the EMA: validation metrics are computed on EMA weights and
a published checkpoint may be the EMA copy, so matching their *final released weights* is a
separate claim from matching their update rule, and we have no EMA at all. Any gradient error
that is a uniform per-tensor scaling, if instrument A
were ever dropped — Adam cancels it and no trajectory of any length recovers it (§7a-bis).
Stability over a real 100k-step run. Precision drift accumulating over
thousands of steps, which a 20-step trajectory cannot observe by construction. Convergence to the
published weights, or any statement about final model quality. Rare sample types outside the
path-complete set of §6, and any dataset the smallest covering set omits. Behaviour at crops beyond
those the stage configs use. Long-run hardware effects: thermal drift, clock decay under sustained
load, and a card-to-card difference that a short run will not surface.

**The honest claim is: "our training step is their training step, verified per-parameter with full
path coverage."** It is not "we ran their training". No row may write the stronger sentence, and the
campaign's DONE_CHECK rejects it.

If Moritz wants the stronger claim, the cheapest honest route is an addendum rather than a redesign:
a short real run from a published intermediate checkpoint, comparing our loss curve against theirs
over a few hundred steps. That buys evidence about drift, which is exactly what §7 cannot give. It
is scoped but not dispatched; it is the first thing to add if the 20-step result is clean.

## 9. Amendments

Each amendment records the date, the row that asked, the change, and the reason. An amendment made
after the affected number existed is marked as such, and any result it touches is re-run.

**A1 — 2026-09-19, asked by `of3t-reference`, §7 rewritten as §7a/§7b. No number existed yet.**
The row measured that the first optimizer step runs at lr = 0.0 (`last_epoch=-1` makes
`_LRScheduler.__init__` call `step()` once) and pointed out that the first two rungs of the
trajectory therefore carry no information. Accepted, and extended further than asked: the defect
is not confined to two rungs. Over 20 warmup steps the weights move by ~1e-4 relative, so a
relative L2 on `w_k` is dominated by an identical `w_0` and would have read as a pass for any
implementation at all. The compared quantity is now the update `d_k = w_k - w_0`, discrimination
starts at k = 3, and the trajectory is run a second time with `warmup_no_steps` scaled down to
give the growth law a usable dynamic range. This is the protocol's own error, caught by a row,
which is what the correction channel is for.

**A17 — 2026-09-19, raised by `of3t-orchestrator` from `of3t-diffusion`'s boundary capture,
§3c gains a second disqualification and the method that answers it. No bar moves.** A13
disqualified a reference that **cannot reproduce itself**. This is the other failure: a
reference that reproduces perfectly and still **disagrees with the thing it is a reference
for**, by more than the bar.

Measured, not supposed: **their** model against **their own** bundle entries at diffusion
scope reads median **6.444e-02**, worst **4.900e-01**, with **491 of 738 tensors over the
5.0e-02 bar** holding **61.54 %** of the compared squared norm — traced to a **6.735e-03**
forward difference (D19). *A forward gap of 6.7e-03 buys a gradient gap roughly ten times
larger.* So at that scope the published artifact imposes a **floor of 6.4e-02 on any
comparison**, and the §3d per-tensor bar is 5.0e-02: **the floor is above the bar**, and no
result obtained that way carries information about our stack.

**The rule.** When a reference's own replay of a scope exceeds the bar at that scope, a §3d
comparison against the published artifact there is **void, not pessimistic**, and must not be
reported as a measurement of our stack. Measure the floor first; if it is above the bar, say
so and stop.

**The method that answers it, with its precondition.** Capture a **boundary** that puts the
confound upstream: if the parameters in question **appear nowhere else in the graph**, the
loss gradient with respect to them *is* the local function driven by the cotangent at that
boundary, so recording `(inputs, output, dL/doutput)` yields a self-contained reference with
the upstream disagreement excluded **by construction rather than by tolerance**. The
precondition is the whole of it and must be checked, not assumed — a parameter that also
feeds another path makes the captured cotangent an incomplete gradient, and the comparison
would be wrong in the flattering direction.

Applied here it converts **89.2106 %** of the squared gradient norm from unmeasurable to
measurable. (Measured on the 0.4.3 reference at pass 151; the 91.21 %
this sentence used to carry was the 0.5.0 / 4,147 bundle that pass 91 disqualified. **And it
used to end "while D19 stays open" — D19 CLOSED at pass 196 on its own pre-registered
branch, so the clause no longer rests on anything; corrected at pass 258, D142.**)

**A16 — 2026-09-19, raised by `of3t-orchestrator` from `of3t-gradients`' stack-scope run, §3d
and §3e gain a reporting requirement. No bar moves; what a FAILING number is allowed to mean
is constrained.** Every §3d comparison must report its **measured zero-model baseline**
alongside its median, and **a median at or above that baseline is a CEILING, not a failure**.

The campaign's standing question has always been *"which check fails if our model is replaced
by zeros?"*. At stack scope it got an answer nobody had planned for: all 48 pairformer blocks,
2,496 of 2,736 tensors, shipped median **1.8986** and `transpose_bias`-off **5.7014** — and
the zero model reads **1.0**. **Both arms score worse than a deleted model.** A per-tensor
relative check cannot distinguish our stack from an absent one there, so quoting 1.8986 as
"the gradient disagrees by 190 %" would be reading a number that carries no information about
the model at all.

The same shape had already appeared against a *reference*: the withdrawn train-mode tape
scored **1.0960 against a zero model's 1.0000**, with **171 of 171 tensors over bar in both
arms** — the over-bar count could not tell them apart and only the median beside a measured
baseline could.

So, binding from here:
  (i)  report the zero-model baseline as a **measurement**, not as the theoretical 1.0 — it is
       a property of the comparison, and on a normalised relative L2 it lands near 1 only when
       the reference's scale is what the relative divides by.
  (ii) a median at or above it is reported as a **ceiling on the instrument at that scope**,
       and the report must then say what *would* discriminate. In this case the forward did:
       one block's masked z error of 7.811e-03 composing to 2.792e-01 over 48 blocks,
       near-linearly, with the disagreement 39.7x and 95.2x above upstream's own replay floor.
  (iii) a ceiling is a **result** and is published as one. It is not a failed measurement, and
       it is not a pass.

**A15 — 2026-09-19, raised by `of3t-orchestrator` from D17's closure, §3d gains a reporting
requirement and the gate enforces it. No bar changes; what a §3d number MEANS is pinned.**
Every §3d figure must state **what fraction of the reference's squared gradient norm its
compared set holds**, beside the count denominator it already owes (K29).

The count denominator is not a scope statement, and this campaign has the measurement that
proves it: 3,275 of 4,147 tensors is **79 % by count and 6.54 % of the squared norm**, because

magnitude, whatever its per-tensor result* — and read the other way, the device bijection's

**A14 — 2026-09-19, raised by `of3t-orchestrator` from `of3t-gradients`' first block-scope
run, §3b and §3e sharpened. A number existed and the amendment REMOVES it from the headline:
the worst per-tensor figure goes from 1.142e+13 to 0.952.** Two failures of a relative bar,
both visible in one artifact.

  (i)  **A relative error needs a denominator floor, and §3b's "zero matches zero" does not
       supply it.** The worst tensor read **1.142e+13** — on a reference gradient whose norm is
       **1.4215e-19**. §3b exempts exactly-zero references; 1.4e-19 is not exactly zero, so it
       passed through and produced a number thirteen orders above the bar that means nothing
       about agreement. Exactly one tensor of 53 was affected, and removing it leaves the worst
       at **0.952** and the median **unchanged at 0.0781** — so the verdict does not move, but
       the headline does, and a headline is what gets quoted. **A comparison must declare a
       denominator floor relative to the reference set's own scale** (here the median ref_norm
       is 2.9e-03, so 1.4e-19 is sixteen orders below its own population) and report tensors
       under it as UNMEASURABLE-AT-THIS-SCALE with their absolute values, never as a relative.

  (ii) **§3e's "perturb by 1 %" is not a control unless 1 % can cross the bar.** On the best
       tensor the baseline relative is 0.0158 against a 0.05 bar; the protocol's 1 % scaling
       moved it to **0.0143 — down, and it did not fire.** The row calibrated to x1.10 (0.0930,
       fires) and kept the zeroed control (1.0, fires). The rule is now: **the perturbation is
       sized against the MEASURED baseline and the bar, and the sizing is reported.** A fixed
       1 % is an assumption about a headroom that has to be checked each time.

**A13 — 2026-09-19, raised by `of3t-orchestrator` from `of3t-gradients`' dropout probe, §3c
gains a precondition on any frozen reference. No bar changes; a reference is disqualified.**
Before a frozen artifact may be used as the right-hand side of a §3d comparison, **its own
reproducibility floor must be measured, and that floor must sit under the bar it will be judged
at.** The detector is one run with the stochastic path disabled, twice.

BUNDLE-MIN fails this. It was taped in **train mode** and its Pairformer block carries one
`Dropout` at rate **0.25**, and the mask is drawn from generators an RNG-state snapshot does not
reproduce across devices. Two seeds on the identical captured boundary: worst **1.167**, median
**0.550**, 47 of 57 over the 0.05 bar; a second pair worst 2.419, median 0.481. With dropout
disabled, two runs are **bit-identical — 0.000e+00 worst and median over 57 of 57**, which is
what identifies dropout as the whole of it. **The artifact's own draw-to-draw floor is an order
of magnitude above the bar it would be judged at**, so a per-parameter comparison against it
measures a mask.

Three consequences, and the second is the one that costs:
  - a bar is **not** wrong because a reference is noisier than it. No tolerance was touched.
  - the published bundle must be **republished with `Dropout` in eval** — one line in
    `bundle_min.py` — and re-hashed. `of3t-reference` is reopened for it.
  - their FD validation **stands**: it restores the same state on the same device per
    evaluation, so the mask is fixed inside that run. A reference can be internally consistent
    and still be unreproducible from the outside, and only the second property makes it a
    reference.

Also recorded: `tt_bio/train/lora.py:46` states the tape has no dropout op, so our stack
computes the r = 0 function regardless — which is why the comparison is legitimate at all once
their side is put in eval, and why nobody noticed for thirty-nine passes.

**A12 — 2026-09-19, raised by `of3t-orchestrator` from its own compose failure, §4 and §5
gain a seam requirement. A number existed and did not move: the gated §5 figure is 7.455e-08
against the unchanged 1e-06 bar.** §4 and §5 were each correct about their own half and the
defect lived between them. §4 drives upstream's real `AlphaFoldLRScheduler` and compares
`theirs[k]` against `af3_lr(k)` — a complete proof of the schedule **as a function**, over
109,005 steps, exact. §5 compared trajectories, and gated the comparison on **our own** index
mapping (update k at `lr(k)`), printing upstream's as "info". So the function was proved, the
optimizer was proved, and **the mapping from update number to schedule argument was proved by
neither** — which is exactly where D11 sat for thirty passes.

Sharper still: §4's reference deliberately never steps the optimizer, and suppresses torch's
ordering warning with the comment that it "says nothing about the schedule". Correct for §4's
scope. That warning is the one diagnostic in either instrument that names the ordering, and
after §4 silenced it and §5 mis-gated it, nothing in the campaign was reading it.

The requirement, in advance and falsifiably:

  (i)  §5 must gate on **upstream's** index mapping, and the mapping must be established by
       running upstream's own objects — driving a real optimizer through a real scheduler and
       recording which lr each update multiplies by — not by reading either side's source and
       arguing. For OpenFold3 that is lr **0, 1.8e-06, 3.6e-06, 5.4e-06, 7.2e-06** at updates
       1..5 (`last_epoch=-1` makes `_LRScheduler.__init__` step once to 0 before training), so
       their update k runs at `lr(k-1)` and their first update runs at exactly 0.
  (ii) Wherever this protocol FACTORS a quantity across instruments — and §1's whole design is
       such a factorisation, four components verified without a card — the factorisation
       itself is a claim that must be checked. Each instrument states what its neighbour is
       assumed to prove, and the composition is owned by something. An unowned seam passes
       every instrument and proves nothing about the product.

This is the protocol's own error in its central design move, and the only reason it surfaced is
that a row fixed the defect and the mis-gated arm inverted. A gate that has never been watched
fail (§3e) and a gate that grades the arm agreeing with us are the same failure wearing
different clothes.

**A18 — 2026-09-19, raised by the device arm of instrument A (`of3t-diffusion`, pass 79),
bounding A16. A number already existed: median 0.7672 against a zero-model baseline of 1.0.**

A16 says that a median at or above the measured zero-model baseline is a **CEILING**, published
as a result rather than retried until it looks better. That rule exists to stop a row grinding a
disappointing number into a pleasing one. It must not become the opposite licence — **publishing
the output of an instrument you already know is incomplete, because A16 said to publish.**

The device arm's first reading is the case. 283 tensors, **median relative L2 0.7672, worst
87.82, 283 of 283 over the 5.0e-02 bar, zero-model baseline 1.0** — a **1.30x** separation from a
deleted model. Under A16 alone that publishes as a ceiling. It must not, because the row can name
two specific defects in the instrument that would produce exactly that number:

1. **The bijection reaches 283 of 870 reachable device weights** (283 of the reference's 738).
   Three load sites were patched; the diffusion transformer, the decoder and the noisy-position
   embedder load by paths none of them cover. An incomplete name map is not a base for a
   model-scope claim.
2. **0.77 is the wrong shape for a precision disagreement.** An fp32-against-float64 gap reads
   ~1e-2. A median sitting at the zero-model baseline with a worst of 87.8 is the signature of a
   **mis-wired operand**, not of arithmetic.

**The rule.** A ceiling is publishable only from an instrument whose completeness you can
assert. The discriminating question is: *can you name a specific defect in the instrument that
would produce this reading?* If you can, you have a broken instrument and the obligation is to
fix it. If you cannot — after looking — you have a ceiling and the obligation is to publish it.
A16 forbids retrying a measurement to improve the number; it does not forbid, and here requires,
**repairing the instrument and measuring again.** The repair must be specified and its expected
effect stated **before** the re-run, so that "fix the instrument" cannot itself become the
grinding A16 exists to stop.

**And the discriminator must be the cheap one.** Here it is the *forward*: `sub_boundary.pt`
already holds their `xl_out` at exactly these inputs, so comparing our `xl_out` against it
separates a wiring defect from a genuine gradient gap in one short run — before any further
gradient work is worth doing. **A gradient instrument must be gated on the forward at its own
boundary agreeing first.** This is D19's lesson (a gradient comparison is never tighter than the
forward it is taken at) applied at the sub-boundary the comparison actually uses, and the device
arm skipped it.

**A18 (addendum) — 2026-09-19, same pass, correcting my own clause before a row acts on it. The
number already existed, in D9, since pass 47.**

A18's second clause says *a gradient instrument must be gated on the forward at its own boundary
agreeing first.* That is right as a **necessary** condition and I wrote it without saying it is
**not a sufficient** one. A row reading it as "forward agrees, therefore proceed with
confidence" would be reading in a guarantee the campaign has already measured to be false.

**D9 is the counterexample and it is ours.** Same module, same probe, same reference, one flag:
`fp32_softmax` moves `tri_att_start`'s weight gradient **1.389e-01 → 4.283e-02** and
`tri_att_end`'s **1.449e-01 → 5.239e-02** — a **3.2x** change — while the corresponding forwards
move **2.610e-02 → 2.923e-02** and **2.390e-02 → 2.677e-02**, about **12 %**. A 3.2x gradient
change hiding under a 12 % forward change is, in D9's own words, *the shape of error a forward
comparison structurally cannot see.*

**A18 ADDENDUM — 2026-09-21 (pass 258), D142. The example above calls D9 a "3.2x gradient
defect". It is not one any more, the arithmetic is untouched, and the lesson is STRONGER for it.**
D9 was RESOLVED at pass 220 as a **policy mismatch**: `openfold3_trunk.py` ships
`fp32_softmax=True` while 0.4.3 runs that softmax in **bf16**, so the 3.2x measured with the flag
off is a move *toward* 0.4.3's own policy, and our fp32 softmax is **3.2x MORE accurate** than
upstream's bf16 one (5.110116e-04 against 1.617567e-03). Every number in the worked example stands
— 1.389e-01 → 4.283e-02, 1.449e-01 → 5.239e-02, forwards moving about 12 %.

**Read the example for what it now shows, which is more than it was written to show.** A 12 %
forward change concealed a 3.2x gradient change that turned out not to be a defect at all. So a
forward comparison cannot distinguish a defect from a deliberate policy difference **or** tell you
which side of the reference you are on — it did not even reveal that the port was the more accurate
one. That is a sharper statement of "necessary, never sufficient" than the original, and it is why
the clause is corrected in place rather than deleted.

**So the clause reads, in full:** a disagreeing forward invalidates the gradient comparison taken
at it, and must be resolved first — that is why the gate exists. **An agreeing forward clears
nothing.** It removes mis-wiring and gross input mismatch from the list; it does not bound the
gradient error, and a `softmax` dtype, an accumulation order, or a backward-only kernel can sit
entirely inside an agreeing forward. Any report that passes the forward gate must say that it
passed a **necessary** condition, and must not describe the path as verified.

This is the campaign's own recurring shape rather than a new caution: **the check that would
have caught it was run at the wrong altitude.** D9 found a 3.2x gradient defect precisely
because somebody stopped trusting the forward.

**A19 — the A18 discriminator threshold, recalibrated for the post-D23 regime.**

**Amended 2026-09-20, orchestrator pass 113, BEFORE the number existed.** Recorded here rather
than in a row's brief because it changes how a bar is read, and §9's rule is that any amendment
says whether a number already existed when it was made. **It did not**: the 0.4.3
`sub_boundary.pt` landed at 01:43:36Z and the discriminator had not been run.

**The problem.** `of3t-rebase`'s brief sets A18's gate as *"~1e-2 or better → wiring sound,
proceed to the gradient"* and *"~1e-1 or worse → a mis-wired operand, do not touch the gradient"*.
The 0.4.3 depth ladder reads **2.168e-02 over 24 blocks**, and `xl_out` is the DiT's output after
those blocks, so the discriminator is expected around **~2.2e-02** — **in neither branch**. A
number that lands between two thresholds, interpreted afterwards, is precisely what fixing
tolerances in advance is meant to prevent.

**The recalibration, and its reasoning.** A18's first clause is *"a disagreeing forward
invalidates the gradient comparison taken at it"*. The operative meaning of **disagreeing** should
be **outside the bar the comparison will be judged at**, which is §3d's per-tensor **5.0e-02** —
not 1e-2. The 1e-2 figure was written when the forward read 1.114e-01 against the 0.5.0 boundary
and the only question was whether it was an order of magnitude out. It was never calibrated for a
regime where D23 has closed and the forward agrees inside the bar.

| discriminator reads | action |
|---|---|
| **< 5.0e-02** | forward agrees at the bar the comparison is judged at — **take the gradient**, and report the forward beside it as the floor under it |
| **5.0e-02 to 1e-1** | take the gradient and state plainly that the forward is over the per-tensor bar, so the gradient number is **bounded rather than measured** |
| **>= 1e-1** | the brief's mis-wired-operand branch, unchanged — do not touch the gradient, localise |

**And the forward is a floor, not a prediction of the gradient.** D9 measured a **3.2x** shift in
the triangle-attention weight gradient under a **12 %** change in the corresponding forward, so a
2e-02 forward does not imply a 2e-02 gradient. Whatever the discriminator reads is reported
*beside* the gradient as its floor and never *as* an expectation for it.


**A20 — 2026-09-20, raised by `of3t-orchestrator` (pass 118), A15's denominator rule. No number
changes; one number is restated.** A15 says reach must be reported as a share of squared gradient
norm rather than as a count of tensors. It did not say what happens to a tensor the instrument
could not compare at all. Instrument A currently drops such tensors into `absent`, and `absent`
leaves the denominator, so the reported share is a share of what the instrument happened to see
rather than of what it was asked to cover.

This is not hypothetical. At pairformer block 47,
`attn_pair_bias.linear_z.weight` carries 26.12 % of the block's reference gradient mass; under
`scale_pair_bias=False` it is compared and fails at 0.811, and under the shipped
`scale_pair_bias=True` the value-bijection cannot place it and it becomes `absent`. The reported
reach of 12.336 % is a reach of **9.114 %** against the full block. The lever changed what the
measurement could see, in the direction that flatters it, and nothing in the output said so.

**The rule.** A reach figure must name its denominator, and the denominator is the **full
reference mass in scope**, not the compared subset. A tensor present in the reference and absent
from the comparison counts as **unreached**, never as not-there. Where a reference norm for an
absent tensor genuinely cannot be obtained, the reach must be published as a bound — *"at most X %
of the scope was compared"* — and the uncompared share stated alongside.

**Why it is a protocol rule and not a row's bug.** Every instrument in this campaign reports a
bijection with an `absent` list, and every one of them computes its share over the placed
tensors. The failure mode is structural: the harder a transform is to match by value, the more
likely its tensors are to vanish from the denominator, so the instrument is least able to see
exactly the changes most likely to be wrong.

Consequence for figures already on the record: block-level reach figures quoted before pass 118
are reaches of the compared set. They are not retracted — they are correct statements about the
set they describe — but they are upper bounds on reach against the full scope, and any figure
used to argue that a section is covered must be restated against the full denominator first.

**A21 — 2026-09-20, raised by `of3t-orchestrator` (pass 138), the homogeneity test and what it
does and does not establish. No number changes; one claim of mine is narrowed.** A backward pass
is linear in the output cotangent for a fixed forward, and the forward recomputations inside it do
not depend on the cotangent. So scaling the injected cotangent by `k` and the stored reference by
the same `k` leaves `norm_ratio` and `cos` **invariant in exact arithmetic**.

**[THIS PARAGRAPH IS WRONG AND IS REPLACED BY A22. The sentence it carried — "choose `k` a power
of two and the test has no noise floor" — is removed rather than annotated, because a wrong
instruction sitting in a protocol gets followed. Powers of two make the arm VACUOUS: shifting
every exponent and leaving every mantissa untouched means the result is invariant *by the
arithmetic*, whatever the defect is, so the arm cannot fail. See A22.]**

**What movement establishes, and what it does not.** It establishes that the backward is **not
homogeneous**. Three mechanisms do that and they are different defects: denormal flush or
underflow; overflow or saturation; and a **fixed additive epsilon, clamp or threshold**, which
breaks homogeneity at *any* magnitude and has nothing to do with the arm being large. Pass 137's
wording — *"any movement is finite-precision magnitude dependence"* — is **narrowed here**: it
excludes the third, and the third is the one that would be a plain bug rather than a precision
limit.

**Separating them costs one ladder rather than one point.** Run `k` both ways — 8, 4, 2, 1, 1/2,
1/4, 1/8, 1/16. Movement only as `k` falls is underflow; only as `k` rises is saturation; movement
in both directions that *shrinks* as `|log k|` grows is a fixed epsilon, because an additive term
is relatively largest when the signal is smallest.

**And a homogeneity test needs a passing control.** Run the same ladder at a block the instrument
calls clean. If the clean block also moves, the non-homogeneity is everywhere and the failing
block merely has enough of it to show; if the clean block is bit-identical across the ladder and
the failing one is not, the non-homogeneity is specific to it. Without the control a positive
result at the failing block alone cannot distinguish those, and the stronger reading is the one
that would be quoted.


**A22 — 2026-09-20, raised by `of3t-rebase` and confirmed by `of3t-orchestrator` (pass 142). A21's
central instruction was backwards. One number changes: none; one arm is re-read as empty.**

A21 said to choose `k` a power of two so the scaling is exact and the test has no noise floor.
**That is exactly the choice that makes the arm incapable of failing.** Scaling every input of a
linear floating-point computation by `2^n` shifts exponents only: every mantissa and every
rounding decision is untouched, so the result is invariant **by the arithmetic**, whatever defect
is present. The same holds for bf16 and for block-float formats with a per-tile shared exponent.
Ordinary rounding error is *relative*, so it is exactly scale-invariant under `2^n` — which means
a power-of-two ladder cannot see the magnitude-dependent rounding the test was written to find.

**Measured, at block 47:**

| `k` | power of two | median `rel` | pair `r` | single `r` | `cos` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.0 | yes | 0.201289 | 1.183174 | 0.886707 | 0.997679 |
| 0.125 | yes | 0.201289 | 1.183174 | 0.886707 | 0.997679 |
| 0.015625 | yes | 0.201289 | 1.183174 | 0.886707 | 0.997679 |
| 0.1 | **no** | 0.202049 | 1.183496 | 0.887574 | 0.997702 |
| 0.0137 | **no** | 0.201675 | 1.183135 | 0.885709 | 0.997708 |

The three powers of two agree to **all six digits across a 64x range**. That is the vacuity, and
it is visible in the artifact.

**The rule.** Scale-invariance arms use scales with **dirty mantissas** — 0.1, 0.0137, 3.7. Keep
the powers of two as a separate **arithmetic control**: they *must* read bit-identical, and if
they do not, the computation is not linear in that input and nothing else in the experiment can
be read. Here they did, so linearity is established and the non-power arms are interpretable.

**The failure mode this belongs to.** Choosing the scale for exactness selects exactly the case
that cannot fail. It is a negative control that does not break what the check reads, arriving from
the opposite direction — the *positive* arm was made incapable of moving.

**What survives.** The conclusion is unchanged and now rests on evidence: across a **73x** range
(1.0 to 0.0137) the pair factor moves **0.03 %** and the single **0.2 %**, while they sit **18 %**
and **11 %** from unity. **Gradient magnitude does not drive the block-47 factors.** The
pass-141 reading stands; the pass-138 evidence for it was empty.

**A23 — 2026-09-20, raised by `of3t-orchestrator` (pass 151). A median over tensors is a
statistic about the tensors that carry no mass. Every set statistic must be reported with the
fraction of reference mass its set holds, and a mass-concentrated scope may not be headlined by
a median-over-tensors.**

Measured exhaustively on the 0.4.3 reference (4,170 tensors, model squared gradient norm
10.279642678524985):

| reaching | tensors | % by count |
|---|---|---|
| 50 % of the gradient's mass | **8** | 0.19 % |
| 90 % | **52** | 1.25 % |
| 99 % | 628 | 15.06 % |
| 99.9 % | 1,814 | 43.50 % |

The **median** tensor holds **1.305e-04 %** of the model's mass. The 2,085 tensors at or below
the median — the half a median-over-tensors statistic is centred on — hold **0.05746 %** of the
mass between them, one part in 1,740.

**So the campaign's own 2.0e-02 median-over-tensors bar is a bar evaluated where the gradient
is not.** That is not a reason to drop it: it is a good per-tensor safety net, it catches
structural breakage, and it is scope-independent. It is a reason it cannot be the headline. A
change that moves the median-over-tensors and leaves the heavy tensors alone has changed
almost nothing about the gradient vector; a change that moves one of the top eight and leaves
the median alone has changed half of it.

**The rule.**

1. Any statistic computed over a set of tensors is reported **with the fraction of the
   reference's squared norm that set holds**. "median 7.11e-01 over 98 tensors" becomes
   "median 7.11e-01 over 98 tensors holding 5.5589 % of the model".
2. For any scope, the **headline** number is a mass-weighted one — `rel_l2` over the
   concatenated set, or the mass-weighted share in agreement. The median-over-tensors is
   reported **beside** it, never instead of it.
3. When a scope's mass is concentrated in a few tensors, **name them and give their individual
   results**. `aux_heads` is the extreme case: `aux_heads.distogram.linear.weight` is
   **100.0000 %** of that section's mass and the other 243 tensors hold 0.000001 % of the model
   between them. A median over those 244 is a median over 243 numbers that mean nothing.

**And it exposes a gap in A14.** A14 excludes tensors with `ref_norm < 1e-12`. That removes 86
tensors holding 1.1e-23 % of the mass — the exact zeros. It does **not** remove the 196 tensors
with `ref_norm < 1e-6`, which hold 2.0e-10 % of the mass and are, for every purpose a parity
claim has, also zero. A14's threshold was set to avoid dividing by zero. The threshold that
matters is **mass**, not norm, and it is rule 1 above, not a larger epsilon: do not exclude
them, **weight** them.

**What this re-scores.** D49's `fp32_softmax=False` result was scored as "three blocks cross the
median bar, 5 of 7 pass against 2". Those seven pairformer blocks hold roughly 0.5 % of the
model's mass between them, and the statistic that moved was the median-over-tensors within each.
The measurement stands exactly as taken; what it licenses is narrower than the phrasing
suggested, and the lever's effect on the model's gradient as a vector is **unmeasured**. The same
applies to every per-block §3d figure this campaign has produced.

Record: `perf/of3t_orchestrator/WHERE_THE_GRADIENT_MASS_LIVES.json`,
`perf/of3t_orchestrator/BLOCK_MASS_PROFILE.json`. Filed as D51.

**A24 — 2026-09-20, raised by `of3t-orchestrator` (pass 175). An input to a measurement is
identified by its DIGEST, not by its path, and the digest belongs in the result.**

A brief that names a reference by filesystem path has pinned nothing. A path is a name for
whatever is at that name *when the row happens to read it*, and in a fleet where several rows run
at once that is not a constant.

This is not hypothetical. `of3t-trajectory` was dispatched at 10:46 to compare our device
gradient against `/home/ttuser/of3t_refprec/run/arm4_bf16_autocast/grads_f64.pt`. Six minutes
later `of3t-refprec` — whose own it1 had been killed at the 3000 s turn cap with no JSON — was
found re-running all four arms into that same directory. The 2.95 GB reference was about
twenty-eight minutes from being rewritten in place. `torch.save` truncates the path it opens;
there is no atomic rename to hide behind.

**The failure mode is what makes this a protocol rule rather than a scheduling note.** A read
that lands on a short file raises, and a raise is harmless — you lose the run and rerun it. A
read that lands on a file whose header is new and whose tail is old, or that completes against a
fully rewritten file that differs from the one every other number in the campaign was scored
against, produces **a number that looks exactly like a measurement**. Nothing downstream can tell
the difference, because the only record of what was read is a path that still exists.

So, for every measurement:

1. **Pin the input before reading it.** Copy or otherwise fix the bytes if the writer may still
   be alive; a hardlink is *not* sufficient, because truncation of the path hits the shared
   inode.
2. **Record the digest of what was actually read** in the result artifact, next to the number it
   produced. A result whose inputs are named only by path is not reproducible and cannot be
   re-scored later, which is the same reason A15/D17 requires the denominator be written down.
3. **Verify the digest against the expected value before loading, and STOP on a mismatch** rather
   than measuring. A mismatch means the pin was taken against something other than the run the
   surrounding numbers came from; every figure downstream of it would be unattributable.
4. **When one row reads another row's output, check whether the writer is still running.** The
   hazard is introduced by whoever dispatches the reader, so it is the dispatcher's to close.

**And it generalises past files.** A checkpoint, a batch, a draws file and a package *revision*
are all inputs under this rule — the campaign already learned the last of these the hard way,
twice: a reference's code revision is part of the measurement, and a `getattr` fallback that
names a version is indistinguishable from having measured one. A24 is the same rule stated once
for every input rather than re-learned per input type.

Record: D75, `workstreams/of3t-trajectory.txt` AMENDMENT 1 (which carries both pinned sha256s),
`/home/ttuser/of3t_refprec/pinned_p175/`.

**A25 — 2026-09-20, raised by `of3t-orchestrator` (pass 175) after `of3t-direct`'s measurement.
When the reference is itself imprecise, "agrees with the reference" is a STRICTER bar than "is as
accurate as the reference", and both must be reported.**

`of3t-direct` measured `diffusion_conditioning` — **36.9462 %** of the model, the campaign's best
result — against upstream's own bf16 training gradient and it **failed** the bar at **1.0414x**.
Then it reported the geometry, and the geometry inverts the meaning of the failure:

    our error against the float64 ideal        0.015328
    upstream's bf16 error against the ideal    0.121864     <- 8x LARGER than ours
    cos between the two errors                -0.2727      <- weakly ANTI-aligned
    our distance from THEIR gradient           6.463839e-02  vs threshold 6.207149e-02

**Our gradient is eight times more accurate than the training step we are trying to reproduce**,
and it fails a bar of the form *"no further from their gradient than they are from the ideal"* —
because two errors that point different ways **add**. The row put it exactly: the bar "is not 'our
error is small', it is 'our error is smaller than, or aligned with, theirs'." An error of our
magnitude that were merely *independent* would read 1.0079x; the anti-alignment alone carries it
to 1.0414x.

**This is a real bar and it is the right bar for a *trajectory* claim** — if you want to argue our
optimizer step lands where theirs lands, agreement with their step is what matters and direction
counts. But it is the **wrong** bar for an *accuracy* claim, and this campaign's own foundation
says **parity means accuracy, not bit-exactness**. A port that is strictly more accurate than the
reference cannot be said to have failed to reproduce it on accuracy grounds.

So, for every comparison against a reference that is not the ideal:

1. **Report both distances** — from the reference **and** from the ideal — and the reference's own
   distance from the ideal beside them. Three numbers, never one.
2. **Report the cosine between the two error vectors.** It is what decides whether your error sits
   inside the reference's or adds to it, and it is not recoverable from the magnitudes. Where the
   ideal is available this costs nothing extra.
3. **Say which bar a verdict is against.** "Fails agreement with their step at 1.0414x while being
   8x more accurate than it" is one sentence and it is the result; either half alone misleads, in
   opposite directions.
4. **Do not upgrade a failure against the reference into a failure of accuracy**, or a pass on
   accuracy into a reproduction claim. A15/D17 already requires the denominator be written down;
   this requires the *subtrahend* be written down too, with its own error.

**What it re-reads.** Every "does not survive the direct test" on this record needs its accuracy
column beside it. `layer_norm_s` at 1.70x and `conditioning` at 1.0414x are **not** the same kind
of result, and the diffusion transformer's 138.8x — where our error is genuinely far larger than
upstream's, not merely misdirected — is a third kind. D72's optimistic reading was wrong to treat
a shared-subtrahend pass as agreement; it does not follow that agreement is the only thing worth
measuring.

**A25 ADDENDUM — 2026-09-20, same pass, forced by A26. The worked example above says
`diffusion_conditioning` "FAILED the bar at 1.0414x". Read A26 before you carry that verdict
anywhere.** The 1.0414x is against the *"equals float64"* threshold, and **A26 shows no bf16 port
can reach that threshold**: two independent error vectors of equal size subtract to **sqrt(2)**
times it. Against the bar a bf16 port can actually reach, **the same measurement passes at
0.7363x**.

A25's substance is unchanged and still required — agreement with an imprecise reference is a
stricter test than accuracy; report three distances and the cosine; say which bar. What changes is
**the verdict on its own example**, and clause 3's model sentence should now read: *"passes the
reachable bar at 0.7363x while being 8x more accurate than the step it reproduces"* rather than
*"fails agreement at 1.0414x while being 8x more accurate"*. Both describe one measurement; the
second scores it against a bar nothing can meet.

This addendum exists because **an amendment that supersedes another's conclusion has to say so
inside it.** A row reads PROTOCOL top to bottom and stops when it has what it needs; leaving the
correction only in A26 means A25 goes on teaching a failure the campaign no longer stands behind.
Same rule as "a superseded stamp does not stop a number being read", applied to protocol rather
than to artifacts.

Record: `of3t-direct` (`f2d29c403`), D72, D76, `of3t-trajectory`'s
`perf/of3t_trajectory/NOTES.md`.

**A26 — 2026-09-20, raised by `of3t-residual` (pass 175) and adopted. The bar for an independent
reimplementation is NOT "equals the ideal". Two independent error vectors of the same size
subtract to sqrt(2) times that, so sqrt(2) x threshold is the bar a port can actually be held to,
and the "equals the ideal" threshold is UNREACHABLE by construction.**

A25 established that when the reference is itself imprecise, agreement with it is a stricter bar
than accuracy. A26 says how much stricter, and it is calculable rather than a matter of taste.

Write `e` for our error against the ideal and `t` for the reference's. What an agreement comparison
measures is `||e - t||`, and

    ||e - t||^2 = ||e||^2 + ||t||^2 - 2<e,t>

so for two implementations of **the same accuracy** whose errors are **independent**
(`||e|| = ||t||`, `<e,t> = 0`), the reading is `sqrt(2) ||t||` — **not zero, and not `||t||`**. On
the diffusion scope that is

    "equals float64" threshold          5.750945e-02     unreachable for any bf16 port
    independent, same accuracy          8.133064e-02     = sqrt(2) x threshold
    of3t-residual's bounded arm         7.777580e-02     = 0.9563x that bar

**and the residual is arithmetic, not a defect.** Our bounded error is 5.930664e-02 from float64
against upstream's 5.852018e-02 — a ratio of **1.0134** — with the two error vectors nearly
orthogonal at **cos +0.0977**. That predicts
`sqrt(1.0134^2 + 1 - 2*1.0134*0.0977) * 5.750945e-02 = 7.77768e-02` against a **measured
7.777580e-02**: agreement to **1.26e-05 relative**. The distance that survives an accurate softmax
is the consequence of subtracting two independent bf16 error vectors of the same size, and **no
work on our side of the comparison can remove it.**

`of3t-residual` demonstrated that directly and it is the most useful negative result of the pass:
bounding the transition path on top of the softmax removed **35 %** of our own error — distance
from float64 5.930664e-02 to 3.815464e-02, per-tensor count over the 5.0e-02 bar from 295 of 547
to **43 of 547** — and bought **0.57 %** of agreement. Getting *more accurate than the reference*
does not get you *closer to the reference*.

So, for any agreement claim against an imprecise reference:

1. **State the sqrt(2) bar beside the "equals the ideal" threshold**, and score against the one a
   port can reach. Quoting only the unreachable one manufactures a failure — D76's mistake in a
   subtler form: not an unreachable *branch*, an unreachable *bar*.
2. **Predict the agreement from the three measured quantities** — `||e||`, `||t||`, `cos(e,t)` —
   and report the prediction beside the measurement. If they agree, the gap is geometry and there
   is nothing to fix; if they disagree, *that* difference is the defect, and it is smaller than the
   raw gap.
3. **Do not spend effort reducing `||e||` below `||t||`** in pursuit of agreement. Past that point
   the reading is dominated by `||t||` and improvements are invisible. Say so rather than
   optimising into it.
4. **The sqrt(2) applies only to independent errors of equal size.** With a measured `cos` and
   ratio, use the full expression above; sqrt(2) is the special case, quoted because it is the
   right order-of-magnitude sanity check.

**What A26 does not license.** It is not permission to stop measuring: a port whose error is
*larger* than the reference's still fails on accuracy (the diffusion transformer at 129x), and a
port whose error is *anti-aligned* reads worse than sqrt(2) even at equal size — `diffusion_
conditioning` at cos -0.273 is the case, and `of3t-residual`'s own transition-bounded arm flips to
cos -0.2938, which is why its agreement barely improved while its accuracy improved 1.55x.

Record: `of3t-residual`'s A25 field and `perf/of3t_residual/`, PROTOCOL A25, D76, D86.

**A24-AMENDMENT — 2026-09-20, forced by `of3t-pairformer` (pass 175, D88). A digest pins the
BYTES, not the FUNCTION. Two gradients of different losses produce a finite, plausible, entirely
meaningless relative error, and no amount of digest discipline detects it.**

A24 requires every input be identified by digest, verified before loading and recorded. That is
necessary and it is **not sufficient**. At pass 175 I dispatched a row to score the pairformer
trunk against a pinned reference whose sha256 matched exactly — and which was the gradient of a
**different step**: arm4 at loss 1.267624369070698 against the only available trunk boundary at
loss 1.6591175475821072. The row verified the digest, refused the reference, and built one over
its own boundary with upstream's own module and recipe so that all arms share one function by
construction.

So, added to A24: **before scoring, assert that both sides are functions of the same loss**, by
whichever of these the scope allows —

1. **bit-identity of a shared intermediate** — `of3t-trajectory` asserts `diffcap043`'s `grad_f64`
   is bit-identical to the bundle's own float64 gradient over all 547 tensors, max abs diff 0.0,
   and says why: *without it our gradient and arm4's are not gradients of the same loss*;
2. **the loss value and the gradient's global norm**, recorded on both sides and compared — the
   two numbers that caught D88, and they are free;
3. **construction** — compute the reference over the **same captured boundary** with upstream's
   own module and recipe, which is what `upstream_arm.py` does and is the strongest form, because
   it makes the shared function true by construction rather than by check.

And when a brief names a reference, it must name the **step** the reference is of, not only its
path and digest. A reference is identified by digest **plus the function it differentiates**.
Record: D88, `of3t-pairformer`'s DIGEST field, A24.
